items.title: 56706_Buddy Tate oral history interview
items.q: Then there were a lot of blacks even turned on to Gene Austin

ctx.x: Would it have been unusual for him to run into some young black kids who knew his records at that time?

You know, I don't think so. I think they were more turned on than today to jazz, more young black kids were turned on to jazz then because they didn't have the disco. You either liked blues singers and jazz and, you know, singers like Bessie Smith, blues singers, Mamie Smith, they were the blues singers. Then there were a lot of blacks even turned on to Gene Austin, who -- I think he sold more -- nobody's ever topped his "Blue Heaven," I don't think.
